name_en: Juwari soba — soba noodles made from 100% buckwheat flour, with no wheat binder
summary_ja: そば粉と水だけで打ち、小麦粉などのつなぎを一切使わないそば。生粉打ちそばとも呼ばれる。生地がまとまりにくく切れやすいぶん打ち手の技術が問われるが、そば本来の香りと風味が薄まらずに出るとされる。
summary_en: Soba made from buckwheat flour and water alone, with no wheat flour or other binder added. Also called kikouchi-soba, the dough is fragile and prone to breaking, which demands real skill from the maker, but it is said to let buckwheat's own aroma and flavor come through undiluted.
source_title: 十割 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Nihachi soba — soba noodles mixed at a roughly 8:2 ratio of buckwheat to wheat flour
summary_ja: そば粉八割・小麦粉二割の配合、あるいは「江戸流のそば」を指すとされる呼び名。享保年間にそば史に登場したとされるが、二八の由来には代価説と配合説があり、いまも結論は出ていないという。
summary_en: A name said to denote either a roughly 8:2 ratio of buckwheat to wheat flour, or simply "Edo-style soba" more broadly. It is said to have entered soba's written history in the Kyoho era, though accounts differ on whether the name comes from the blend ratio or from an old noodle price, and no settled answer exists.
source_title: 二八そば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Sotoni — a way of counting the nihachi ratio by adding wheat flour on top of a full measure of buckwheat
summary_ja: 二八そばの配合の数え方の一つ。そば粉十に対して小麦粉二を外側から足す考え方で、そば粉八・小麦粉二を最初から合わせる「内二」と区別される。同じ二八でも、打ち場での計算のしやすさが選び分けの理由とされる。
summary_en: One of two ways of counting the nihachi ratio: sotoni adds two parts wheat flour on top of a full ten parts buckwheat flour, as distinct from uchini, which starts from eight parts buckwheat and two parts wheat. Both are called nihachi, and which one a shop uses is said to come down to which arithmetic is easier at the workbench.
source_title: 外一、外二、内二、二八そば(二八蕎麦)、蕎麦と小麦粉の割合を解説
source_publisher: 日本蕎麦保存会

name_en: Sarashina soba — pale, refined noodles milled from the buckwheat grain's innermost starch
summary_ja: そばの実の中心部だけを挽いた白い「更科粉（一番粉）」で打つそば。甘皮や殻を含まないため色が薄く、そばともそうめんとも違う独特の舌触りになるとされる。江戸中期の文献に初めて登場した高級な粉だという。
summary_en: Soba made from sarashina flour, milled only from the pale starch at the center of the buckwheat grain, with none of the darker husk or bran mixed in. The result is noodles pale enough to look almost white, with a texture said to sit somewhere between ordinary soba and somen. The flour is said to have first appeared in mid-Edo-era writing as a luxury product.
source_title: さらしなそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Inaka soba — thick, dark buckwheat noodles carrying a strong, rustic flavor
summary_ja: 更科そばの対極に位置づけられる、太めで黒っぽくそばらしい味わいの濃いそば。「山家そば」とも呼ばれ、江戸風のそばに対する地方・農山村のそばという意味合いを持つとされる。幕末の江戸にも同名の店があったという。
summary_en: Placed at the opposite end of the spectrum from sarashina soba, inaka soba is thick, dark, and carries a strong buckwheat flavor. Also called yamaga-soba, the name is said to have marked it as rural or mountain-village soba, set against the more refined Edo style. A shop by the same name is said to have existed in Edo itself in the closing years of the shogunate.
source_title: 田舎そば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Hikigurumi — soba flour milled from the whole grain, husk and all
summary_ja: そばの実を、一番粉・二番粉といった段階に取り分けずまるごと挽く製法、またはその粉で打ったそば。殻に近い部分まで挽き込むため色が濃く、香りが強く出るとされる。更科粉とは対極の考え方の粉になるという。
summary_en: Soba flour milled from the whole buckwheat grain — husk and all — without separating it into first-flour, second-flour, and so on by stage. Because it grinds in flour close to the husk, the color runs dark and the aroma comes through strong, sitting at the opposite end of the spectrum from sarashina flour.
source_title: 一番粉 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: The Yabu lineage — one of Edo's three great soba schools, known for a sharp, aromatic bite
summary_ja: 江戸から続くそば屋の系統の一つ。幕末に東京・根津の団子坂にあった「蔦屋」が周りを竹やぶに囲まれていたことから「藪そば」と通称され、それが屋号として定着したとされる。二八の配合を基本とするという。
summary_en: One of the three great soba lineages of Edo. In the closing years of the shogunate, a shop called Tsutaya, near Nezu's Dango-zaka slope, was surrounded by a bamboo thicket — yabu — and came to be known by that nickname, which is said to have settled into its shop name. The lineage is said to work from a base nihachi ratio.
source_title: かんだやぶそば（スポット紹介）
source_publisher: 千代田区観光協会公式サイト Visit Chiyoda

name_en: The Sunaba lineage — an Edo soba school whose roots are said to trace back to Osaka
summary_ja: 江戸から続くそば屋の系統の一つ。名の由来は天正11年（1583年）、大坂城築城の資材置き場「砂場」にあったそば屋にさかのぼるとされる。徳川の世になって江戸へ移り、細く長くつながる喉ごしを持ち味とする系統として広まったという。
summary_en: One of Edo's three great soba lineages. Its name is said to trace back to 1583, to a soba shop standing at a construction-supply yard called Sunaba during the building of Osaka Castle. The lineage is said to have moved to Edo once the Tokugawa took power, becoming known for a thin, long, smoothly sliding noodle.
source_title: 砂場の歴史
source_publisher: 虎ノ門 大坂屋 砂場

name_en: The Sarashina lineage — the Edo soba school built on pale, refined sarashina flour
summary_ja: 江戸から続くそば屋の系統の一つ。寛政元年（1789年）、信州出身の初代が江戸麻布永坂町に「信州更科蕎麦所 布屋太兵衛」の看板を掲げたのが始まりとされる。白いさらしなそばと、彩り豊かな変わりそばを看板商品としてきたという。
summary_en: One of Edo's three great soba lineages. It is said to trace back to 1789, when a man from Shinshu hung a sign reading "Shinshu Sarashina Soba Shop, Nunoya Tahei" in Azabu Nagasaka-cho, Edo. The lineage is said to have built its name on pale sarashina soba alongside colorful kawari-soba.
source_title: 更科堀井について
source_publisher: 総本家 更科堀井

name_en: Kawari-soba — soba dough flavored or colored with a second ingredient kneaded in
summary_ja: そば粉の生地に茶や卵、山菜など別の材料を練り込んで香りや色を添えたそば。色が鮮やかなものはとくに「色物」と呼んで区別するという。江戸時代の玉子蕎麦切りが最も古い例とされ、文化文政期に遊び心のあるそばとして広まった。
summary_en: Soba whose dough has a second ingredient — tea, egg, wild greens, and the like — kneaded in for color or aroma. Noodles with especially vivid color are singled out and called irimono. The oldest known example is said to be tamago-sobakiri, an egg noodle from the Edo period, and the practice is said to have flourished as a playful variation during the Bunka-Bunsei era.
source_title: 変わりそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Cha-soba — soba noodles kneaded with powdered green tea
summary_ja: そば粉の生地に抹茶や粉末の緑茶を練り込んだ変わりそば。うっすらとした緑色と茶葉の香りが加わる。文化文政期（1804〜30年）に柚子切りなどと並んで考案された、遊び心のあるそばの一つとされる。
summary_en: A kawari-soba made by kneading powdered green tea, often matcha, into the buckwheat dough. It takes on a faint green tint along with tea's own aroma. It is said to be one of the playful noodle variations devised during the Bunka-Bunsei era (1804–30), alongside yuzu-flavored soba.
source_title: 変わりそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Yuzukiri — soba noodles kneaded with grated yuzu peel for a citrus aroma
summary_ja: そば粉の生地に柚子の皮をすりおろして練り込んだ変わりそば。柚子の香りがそばの香りに重なるのが持ち味とされる。文化文政期（1804〜30年）に茶そばなどと並んで考案された、遊び心のあるそばの一つという。
summary_en: A kawari-soba made by grating yuzu citrus peel into the buckwheat dough. The fruit's aroma is said to layer over buckwheat's own scent as the noodle's main appeal. It is said to be one of the playful variations devised during the Bunka-Bunsei era (1804–30), alongside cha-soba.
source_title: 変わりそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Mori soba and zaru soba — cold soba dipped in sauce, plain or crowned with nori
summary_ja: 茹でて冷水で締めたそばをつゆにつけて食べる、冷たいそばの基本形。「もり」はつゆをかけずつける食べ方を区別する呼び名として広まり、「ざる」はそれより古く、竹ざるに盛ったことに由来するとされる。今は海苔の有無が主な違いという。
summary_en: The basic cold soba: noodles boiled and rinsed in cold water, then dipped in sauce. "Mori" is said to have spread as a name distinguishing the dip-and-eat style from pouring sauce directly over the noodles, while "zaru," older still, is said to trace to noodles served on a bamboo strainer. Today the main difference is said to come down to whether nori is sprinkled on top.
source_title: もりそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Kake soba — hot soba served directly in a bowl of broth
summary_ja: 茹でたそばに直接つゆを注いで食べる、種物の基本形。室町期の文献にはつゆをつけずに直接かける食べ方への戒めが見られ、これが「ぶっかけ」の始まりとされる。江戸後期には男性的な食べ方として広まったという。
summary_en: Hot soba with broth poured directly over it, forming the base for every topped variety. A Muromachi-era text is said to warn against pouring sauce straight onto the noodles rather than dipping, which is taken as evidence that the practice — the root of what became bukkake — already existed. By the late Edo period, it is said to have spread as a more masculine way of eating soba.
source_title: そばの食べ方 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Kamo nanban — hot soba topped with duck meat and scallion
summary_ja: かけそばに鴨肉とねぎをのせた種物。文化年間（1804〜18年）、江戸馬喰町の「笹屋」が最初に商品化したというのが定説とされる。「南蛮」はねぎを好んだ南方の人々を指す江戸時代の呼び名に由来するという。
summary_en: Kake soba topped with duck meat and scallion. The going account credits Sasaya, a soba shop at Bakurocho in Edo, with first putting it on the menu during the Bunka era (1804–18). "Nanban" is said to derive from an Edo-era term for southerners, reputed to favor scallion in their cooking.
source_title: 鴨南蛮 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Tororo soba — cold soba topped with grated mountain yam
summary_ja: すりおろした山の芋をもり汁でのばしたとろろをかけて食べるそば。江戸時代の『蕎麦全書』（1751年）には、山の芋をつなぎとして使う工夫も紹介されている。冷たいそばが本筋とされ、温めると粘りが弱まるという。
summary_en: Soba topped with grated mountain yam thinned with mori-style dipping sauce into a smooth tororo. A mid-18th-century text is said to describe mountain yam being worked into the dough itself as a binder. The dish is said to be built around cold noodles, since heat is said to weaken the yam's characteristic stickiness.
source_title: そばと山の芋 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Tenpura soba — hot soba topped with deep-fried shrimp or other tempura
summary_ja: かけそばに天ぷらをのせた種物。文政10年（1827年）の川柳に詠まれており、少なくともそれ以前からそば屋で売られていたとされる。江戸時代は芝海老の天ぷらが主流で、昭和以降は車海老が主流になったという。
summary_en: Kake soba topped with deep-fried tempura. A senryu poem from 1827 is said to mention it, evidence that it was already sold at soba shops by then at the latest. In the Edo period, shiba shrimp was the standard tempura used, giving way to kuruma prawn from the Showa era onward, it is said.
source_title: 天ぷらそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Sobagaki — a thick paste of buckwheat flour and hot water, eaten by the spoonful
summary_ja: そば粉を熱湯で練った、麺にしないそばの食べ方。醤油やわさび、つゆなどをつけてそのまま食べる。麺の形に切る「そば切り」が広まる以前は、そばといえばこの練った形が主流だったと語られる。
summary_en: Soba flour kneaded with hot water into a thick paste, eaten without ever being cut into noodle strands, dipped in soy sauce, wasabi, or broth. Before soba-kiri, the technique of cutting the dough into thin noodles, spread widely, this kneaded form is said to have been the standard way buckwheat was eaten.
source_title: 手打ちそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Sobayu — the hot water soba is boiled in, drunk with leftover dipping sauce after the meal
summary_ja: もりそばを食べ終えたあと、残ったつゆに加えて飲む、そばの茹で汁。信州で始まった風習が江戸中期の寛延（1748〜51年）ごろに江戸へ広まったとされる。そばのタンパク質の約半分が溶け出ているという。
summary_en: The hot water soba noodles were boiled in, poured into the leftover dipping sauce and drunk once the meal is finished. The custom is said to have started in Shinshu and spread to Edo around the Kanen era (1748–51) in the mid-Edo period. Roughly half of soba's protein is said to dissolve into this water.
source_title: そば湯 | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会

name_en: Toshikoshi soba — soba eaten on New Year's Eve, a custom tied to the turning year
summary_ja: 大晦日の夜に食べる習慣のそば。「年取りそば」「大年そば」とも呼ばれる。細く長く伸びる形から長寿や家運の発展を願う説、切れやすさから一年の苦労を断ち切る説など、由来には複数の説があるとされる。
summary_en: Soba eaten on the night of New Year's Eve, also called toshitori-soba or omisoka-soba. Accounts of its origin vary — one ties the noodle's long, thin shape to a wish for long life and lasting fortune, another to the way soba snaps easily, said to cut off a year's hardships.
source_title: 年越しそば | そばの散歩道
source_publisher: 日本麺類業団体連合会
